content: COG2, also known as Conserved Oligomeric Golgi Complex Subunit 2, is a protein in humans encoded by the COG2 gene. This protein is a component of multiprotein complexes that play a critical role in maintaining the structural integrity of the Golgi apparatus. These complexes are essential for the Golgi's functions in intracellular transport and glycoprotein modification. Several specific complexes have been identified in this context. For example, the Golgi Transport Complex (GTC) is involved in general transport processes within the Golgi. The LDLC complex is specifically associated with glycosylation reactions, while the SEC34 complex is implicated in vesicular transport mechanisms. Model organisms have been utilized to investigate the function of COG2. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Cog2tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was developed as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This initiative is a high-throughput mutagenesis project aimed at creating and distributing animal models of human diseases to researchers worldwide. In this study, both male and female mice underwent a standardized phenotypic screening to assess the effects of COG2 gene deletion. A total of 25 tests were conducted on mutant mice. A significant finding was that no homozygous mutant mice survived past the weaning stage, indicating that the complete loss of COG2 is lethal. The remaining tests were performed on heterozygous mutant adult mice, and no additional significant abnormalities were observed in these animals. Furthermore, COG2 has been demonstrated to interact with other components of the conserved oligomeric Golgi complex, specifically COG4 and COG3. These interactions suggest that COG2 plays a collaborative role within the complex to support Golgi function.
